name: PCOS
shortDescription: A common hormonal condition that can affect periods, skin, and fertility.
overview: Polycystic ovary syndrome is a hormonal imbalance that may cause irregular periods, acne, excess hair growth, weight changes, and ovulation challenges.
whenToVisitDoctor: Visit a doctor if your periods are highly irregular, symptoms worsen, or you are struggling to conceive.

name: Endometriosis
shortDescription: Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus and can cause pain.
overview: Endometriosis can lead to severe menstrual cramps, pelvic pain, heavy bleeding, and discomfort during intimacy or bowel movements.
whenToVisitDoctor: Seek medical care when pain is severe, daily life is affected, or heavy bleeding is persistent.

name: Cervical Cancer
shortDescription: Cancer that begins in the cells of the cervix and is often preventable with screening.
overview: Cervical cancer may develop slowly and is strongly linked to persistent high-risk HPV infection. Screening and vaccination are important prevention tools.
whenToVisitDoctor: See a doctor for any unexplained bleeding, especially after sex or between periods.

name: Breast Cancer
shortDescription: A cancer that starts in breast tissue and benefits from early awareness and screening.
overview: Breast cancer can appear as a new lump, skin changes, nipple changes, or swelling. Early detection improves treatment options.
whenToVisitDoctor: Schedule an exam if you notice a lump, nipple change, or any breast change that does not go away.

name: Ovarian Cysts
shortDescription: Fluid-filled sacs on the ovaries that are often harmless but can cause discomfort.
overview: Most ovarian cysts resolve on their own, but larger or persistent cysts may lead to pain, bloating, and cycle changes.
lifestyleTips: Seek urgent care for sudden severe pain
whenToVisitDoctor: Get urgent help for sudden severe pelvic pain, fainting, or fever with pain.

name: Uterine Fibroids
shortDescription: Noncancerous growths in or on the uterus that may cause heavy or painful periods.
overview: Fibroids are common and can lead to heavy bleeding, pelvic pressure, frequent urination, and back pain.
whenToVisitDoctor: See a doctor if bleeding is soaking pads quickly, pain is severe, or anemia symptoms appear.

name: Anemia
shortDescription: A shortage of healthy red blood cells that can cause fatigue and weakness.
overview: Anemia may be related to low iron, vitamin deficiencies, blood loss, or chronic illness and can affect energy and concentration.
whenToVisitDoctor: Ask for evaluation if fatigue is ongoing, symptoms are worsening, or periods are very heavy.

name: Thyroid Disorders
shortDescription: Conditions where the thyroid makes too much or too little hormone.
overview: Thyroid disorders can affect energy, weight, mood, hair, temperature tolerance, and menstrual regularity.
whenToVisitDoctor: Visit a doctor for unexplained fatigue, weight changes, or menstrual changes that continue.

name: Menstrual Disorders
shortDescription: A group of menstrual concerns such as irregular, painful, or very heavy periods.
overview: Menstrual disorders can be linked to hormonal imbalance, fibroids, endometriosis, stress, thyroid changes, or anemia.
whenToVisitDoctor: See a doctor if bleeding is extremely heavy, cycles stop for months, or pain becomes disabling.

name: Gestational Diabetes
shortDescription: High blood sugar during pregnancy that requires close monitoring and support.
overview: Gestational diabetes can occur during pregnancy and is usually managed with nutrition, activity, and blood sugar monitoring.
whenToVisitDoctor: Follow your prenatal team’s advice closely and report abnormal readings or symptoms quickly.
